newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens says 1995/96 DVFA eps 4.48 DM.
newsitem.headline: Siemens says 1995/96 DVFA eps 4.48 DM.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG said on Thursday its 1995/96 earnings per share were 4.48 marks on Germany's DVFA basis, up from 3.97 marks last year.

Siemens, which in November said it expects no increase in 1996/97 profit from last year's, said on Thursday it expected to show a clear profit increase again in 1997/98. The company said on Thursday it sees 1996/97 profit equal to last year's 2.5 billion marks before extraordinaries.
Siemens said it expects to post lower profit in its components, medical equipment and auto parts businesses, but higher profit in energy, communications and information.
The company said it plans to create a new division, Siemens Financial Services.
It said institutional investors hold 45 percent of its shares, making them the largest group of shareholders.
Siemens said its structural investment in 1995/96 was 760 million marks, down from 2.17 billion the year before. Financial profit was 951 million marks, down from 1.456 billion.
The company said it sees a moderate rise in 1996/97 sales and incoming orders.
Siemens said its domestic workforce would continue to decline, and its non-domestic workforce would exceed its domestic workforce in two years, for the first time.
It said it would reinforce core businesses and sell non-core businesses.
Siemens said its medical equipment division would show a loss in 1996/97, and that its plant construction division remained under pressure, with breakeven in doubt.
Siemens said its components division, which includes semiconductors and has been its biggest earner, would continue to show a clear profit in 1996/97.
